1.word_for_word: विंशे — in the twentieth chapter; प्रावृट्-शरत्-शोभा-वर्णनेन — through the description of the beauties of the rainy season and autumn; वनोचिताः प्रावृट्-क्रीडाः — the rainy-season sports appropriate to the forest; गोप-राम-युजः हरेः — of Hari together with the cowherds and Rāma; निरूप्यन्ते — are described; हेय-आदेय-उपमानेन — by similes of what is to be rejected and accepted; प्रावृट्-शरद्-ऋतु-श्रियोः वर्णनम् — the description of the splendors of the rainy and autumn seasons; अद्भुत-ऐश्वर्य-कृष्ण-लीला-विवक्षया — with the intention of expressing Kṛṣṇa's wondrous and sovereign play
1.translation: In the twentieth chapter, by describing the beauties of the rainy season and autumn, the rainy-season sports of Hari in the forest together with the cowherds and Rāma are presented. The splendors of the rainy and autumn seasons are described through comparisons with things to be rejected and things to be accepted, with the intention of expressing the wondrous majesty of Kṛṣṇa's play.

3.word_for_word: तत्र प्रावृट्-वर्णनम् — here begins the description of the rainy season; ततः इत्य्-आदि द्वा-विंशत्या — in twenty-two verses beginning with 'tataḥ'; सर्वेषां प्राणिनां समुद्भवः उत्पत्तितः जीवनतः च यस्याम् — the season in which all living beings arise, both by birth and by being sustained; सा प्रावृट् — that is the rainy season; विद्योतमानाः परिधयः — shining circles or halos; परिवेष-आदि-शोभा यस्याम् — in which there is the beauty of halos and the like; विस्फुर्जितं सङ्क्षुभितं नभस्-तलं यस्याम् — in which the expanse of sky flashes and resounds in agitation
3.translation: Here begins the description of the rainy season, in twenty-two verses starting with ‘tataḥ.’ The rainy season is that in which living beings come forth and are sustained. Its circles and halos shine beautifully, and the expanse of the sky flashes and resounds with agitation.

4.word_for_word: सान्द्रैः निबिडैः नील-अम्बुदैः — with dense, compact dark clouds; विद्युत्-गर्जित-सहितैः — accompanied by lightning and thunder; आच्छन्नम् — covered; स-गुणं गुणैः आच्छन्नं जीवाख्यम् — like the entity called jīva, endowed with guṇas and covered by them; विद्युत्-गर्जित-अम्बुदानाम् — lightning, thunder and cloud; सत्त्व-रजस्-तमोभिः उपमा — are compared with sattva, rajas and tamas
4.translation: The sky was covered by dense, compact dark clouds accompanied by lightning and thunder. The comparison is with the jīva, who is associated with the guṇas and covered by them: lightning, thunder and cloud are likened respectively to the three guṇas—sattva, rajas and tamas.

5.word_for_word: पर्जन्यः सूर्यः — here parjanya is the sun; स्व-गोभिः — by his own rays; निज-रश्मिभिः — by his own beams; काले — at the proper time; यथोचित-समये — when the appropriate time arrives; राज-उपमा — a comparison with a king; करात् आनतः — taking tax; समये पुनर् दानतः — and then giving it back at the proper time
5.translation: Here ‘parjanya’ refers to the sun. ‘By his own cows’ means by his own rays. ‘At the time’ means at the appropriate season. A comparison with a king is suggested: as a king first takes revenue as tax and later redistributes it at the proper time, so the sun first draws up water and later gives it back as rain.

6.word_for_word: अस्य विश्वस्य प्रीणनम् — that which refreshes this universe; आप्यायन-करम् — causing nourishment and increase; जीवनम् उदकम् — life-giving water; मुमुचुः — the clouds released; कृपालवः यथा — just as compassionate persons; तप्तं जनं निरीक्ष्य — seeing people afflicted by heat; अनुकम्पमानाः — feeling compassion; तद्-आप्यायनाय स्व-जीवनम् अपि त्यजन्ति — give even their own life to revive them; महान्तः मेघाः — the great clouds; तडित्-नेत्रैः विश्वं तप्तं निरीक्ष्य — seeing the scorched world with lightning as their eyes; वायुभिः वेपिताः — shaken by the winds; जीवनं मुमुचुः — released life-giving water
6.translation: The great clouds released water, the life of the world, which refreshes and nourishes it. The comparison is to compassionate people: seeing others scorched and suffering, they are moved by pity and will give even their own life to restore them. In the same way, the great clouds, as though seeing the heated world with lightning for their eyes and being shaken by the winds, released their life-giving water.

7.word_for_word: तपसा ग्रीष्मेण कृशा — emaciated by the austerity that is summer; देव-मीढा — rained upon by the god; पर्जन्य-सिक्ता — sprinkled by rain; वर्षीयसी — greatly increased; उच्छूना पुष्टा — swollen and nourished; काम्यं तपः यस्य — one who performs austerity for a desired end; तस्य तनुः कामान् संप्राप्य यथा — like his body after obtaining the desired objects
7.translation: The earth had grown thin through the austerity of summer; then, rained upon by the god and drenched by the showers, she swelled and became nourished. The comparison is to the body of one who has performed austerity for desired ends and then becomes full and thriving upon obtaining those desires. The explanation extends through verse 8.

8.word_for_word: अनुशुष्यन्त्यः — drying up afterward; अस्वतन्त्रस्य इन्द्रिय-परतन्त्रस्य — of one who is not independent but subject to the senses; स्वतन्त्रस्य निरङ्कुशस्य इति वा — or, of one who is independent and unrestrained
8.translation: ‘Anuśuṣyantyaḥ’ means ‘drying up afterward.’ The comparison may be to a person who lacks independence because he is controlled by the senses; alternatively, ‘svatantra’ may be read in the sense of someone independent and unrestrained.

9.word_for_word: नित्य-कर्म-अवसाने — at the conclusion of the daily rite; आचार्य-निनदं श्रुत्वा — hearing the teacher's call; तत्-शिष्याः यथा अधीयते — just as his pupils begin to recite their lessons; तद्वत् — in the same way
9.translation: The comparison is to pupils who, at the conclusion of the daily rite, hear their teacher's call and begin reciting their lessons.

10.word_for_word: अनुशुष्यतीः — drying up successively; अनुशुष्यन्त्यः — becoming dry; अस्वतन्त्रस्य इन्द्रिय-परतन्त्रस्य — of one dependent upon the senses; स्वतन्त्रस्य निरङ्कुशस्य इति वा — or of one independent and unrestrained
10.translation: ‘Anuśuṣyatīḥ’ means becoming progressively dry. The comparison may be to one who is unfree because he is controlled by the senses, or, under the alternative reading, to one who is independent and unrestrained.

11.word_for_word: हरिभिः नीलैः शष्पैः — with green-blue shoots of young grass; नील-वर्णा — blue-green in color; क्वचित् इन्द्र-गोपैः — in places, by indragopa insects; लोहिता — red; उच्छिलीन्ध्रैः — with mushrooms; छत्राकारैः उद्भिदैः — umbrella-shaped plants springing from the ground; कृत-च्छाया — patterned with their shade/appearance; नृणां राज्ञां श्रीः सेनासम्पद् इव — like a king's splendor consisting in the wealth of his army
11.translation: The earth appeared blue-green with fresh shoots of young grass, red in places with indragopa insects, and variegated by umbrella-shaped mushrooms springing from the ground. Its splendor was like the magnificence of a king displayed through the wealth of his army.

12.word_for_word: क्षेत्राणि इति — with the word 'fields'; तदा हि — for at that time; वृष्टेः अविच्छेदे — when the rain continues uninterruptedly; लसन्तः प्रियङ्गु-आदयः — flourishing priyangu and other crops; मुदं ददति — give joy; विच्छेदे — when the rain breaks off; शुष्यन्तः — drying up; अनुतापं च — cause sorrow
12.translation: The word ‘fields’ is explained as follows: when the rain continues without interruption, priyangu and the other crops flourish and bring joy; when the rain ceases, they dry up and cause distress.

13.word_for_word: अबिभ्रत् अबिभरुः — they bore, they displayed; यथा हरि-निषेवया — just as through service to Hari; हरि-सेवायां प्रवृत्ताः — those who engage in Hari's service; सद्यः एव सर्वे रुचिराः भवन्ति — immediately all become beautiful/pleasing; तस्यां परम-धर्मत्वात् परम-सुखत्वात् च — because it is the supreme dharma and supreme happiness; तद्वत् — so too here
13.translation: ‘Abibhrat’ has the sense ‘they bore’ or ‘displayed.’ The comparison is to service of Hari: all who enter into Hari's service immediately become beautiful and pleasing, because that service is the highest dharma and the highest happiness. So it was with the renewed beauty of the creatures and landscape.

14.word_for_word: कामाक्तम् — affected by desire; काम-वासनायुक्तम् — possessed of sensual longing; श्वसन-ऊर्मि-साम्यम् — this gives the comparison with wind-driven waves; गुणैः विषयैः युज्यते — one becomes joined to the guṇas, the sense objects; सरित्-सङ्गति-साम्यम् — this gives the comparison with rivers joining other waters
14.translation: ‘Kāmāktam’ means affected by desire, possessed of sensual longing; this supplies the comparison with waves stirred by the wind. The statement that one becomes joined with the guṇas—that is, with sense objects—supplies the comparison with rivers joining other bodies of water.

15.word_for_word: अधोक्षज एव चेतः येषाम् — those whose mind is fixed on Adhokṣaja alone; ते — such persons
15.translation: The persons meant are those whose minds are fixed exclusively upon Adhokṣaja.

16.word_for_word: असंस्कृताः — uncultivated; अक्षुण्णाः — untraversed, unbroken; न अभ्यस्यमानाः — not repeatedly used; असंस्कृत-साम्यम् — this is the point of comparison in being uncultivated; कालेन च हताः — obscured/overcome with time; तृण-आच्छादन-साम्यम् — this is the comparison with being covered by grass
16.translation: ‘Asaṃskṛtāḥ’ means uncultivated, untraversed and no longer regularly used; that is one point of the comparison. With the passage of time such paths are obscured, giving the further comparison with their being covered over by grass.

17.word_for_word: यथा कामिन्यः — like lustful women; पुंश्-चल्यः — unchaste women who move from man to man
17.translation: The comparison is to lustful, unchaste women who move from one man to another.

18.word_for_word: निर्गुणम् — without a string; ज्या-रहितम् — lacking the bowstring; अपि गुणिनि गर्जित-शब्दवति अभात् — yet it appeared upon that which possessed a 'guṇa,' namely the sound of thunder; गुण-व्यतिकरात्मके व्यक्ते प्रपञ्चे — in the manifest world whose nature is the intermingling of the guṇas; अगुणवान् निर्गुणः पुरुषः यथा — like the guṇa-less Puruṣa appearing in it
18.translation: ‘Nirguṇa’ first means ‘without a string,’ without the bowstring; nevertheless the bow appeared against something ‘guṇin,’ namely the sky possessing the sound of thunder. The philosophical comparison is to the nirguṇa Puruṣa, who is without the guṇas yet appears in the manifest world whose nature is the mutual interaction of those guṇas.

19.word_for_word: स्व-भासा भासितया अहम्-मत्याः — by the I-notion illuminated by one's own consciousness; स्व-चैतन्येन एव प्रकाशितेन अहङ्कारेण छन्नः जीवः यथा — like the jīva covered by ahaṅkāra, which itself is illuminated only by the jīva's consciousness; यद् वा — or; अहं विद्वान् दाता वेत्ता शूरः इति — 'I am learned, a giver, a knower, a hero'; स्व-प्रतीत्या एव आरोपितया — through an attribution imposed by one's own notion
19.translation: The comparison is to the jīva concealed by ahaṅkāra, the ‘I’-notion, which itself shines only because it is illumined by the jīva's own consciousness. Alternatively, it refers to the self-imposed notions ‘I am learned,’ ‘I am a generous giver,’ ‘I am a knower,’ ‘I am a hero,’ and so forth.

20.word_for_word: मेघ-आगमेन — with the arrival of the clouds; उत्सवः येषाम् — for whom it was a festival; अतः हृष्टाः — therefore they were delighted
20.translation: Because the arrival of the clouds was itself a festival for them, they became delighted.

21.word_for_word: नानात्म-मूर्तयः — having forms of many different kinds; अनेक-रूप-देहाः — bodies of manifold forms
21.translation: ‘Nānātma-mūrtayaḥ’ means possessing bodies of many different forms.

22.word_for_word: अशान्तानि पङ्क-कण्टक-आदि-युक्तानि रोधांसि — banks made unpleasant by mud, thorns and the like; तेषु अपि न्यूषुः नितराम् अवसन् — even there they remained and dwelt continuously; सारसाः चक्रवाकाः — cranes and cakravāka birds; अशान्तानि घोराणि अनुपरतानि वा कृत्यानि येषु — where troublesome, dreadful or unending duties remain; तेषु अपि गृहेषु — even in such houses
22.translation: The riverbanks were unpleasant, filled with mud, thorns and the like, yet cranes and cakravāka birds continued to dwell there. The comparison is with householders who remain in homes even though those homes involve troublesome, harsh and unending duties.

23.word_for_word: ईश्वरे — in the lord; इन्द्रे — in Indra
23.translation: ‘Īśvare’ here means Indra, the lord of the rains.

24.word_for_word: नुन्नाः — impelled; प्रेरिताः — urged onward; आशिषः — blessings; कामान् — desired objects; विश्पतयः — lords of the people; राजानः — kings; वणिजां पतयः वा — or heads of merchant communities; द्विज-ईरिताः — directed by the twice-born; पुरोहितैः उक्ताः — instructed by their priests
24.translation: ‘Nunnāḥ’ means impelled or urged onward. ‘Āśiṣaḥ’ refers to desired blessings or objects. ‘Viśpatayaḥ’ may mean kings, lords of the people, or heads of merchant communities. ‘Dvijeritāḥ’ means that they were directed and instructed by their brāhmaṇa priests.

25.word_for_word: प्रावृषि कृतां क्रीडां वर्णयति — he describes the sports performed during the rains; एवं वनम् इति सप्तभिः — in seven verses beginning 'evaṃ vanam'; वर्षिष्ठम् — most abundant; समृद्धम् — flourishing, prosperous
25.translation: He now describes in seven verses beginning with ‘evaṃ vanam’ the sports Kṛṣṇa performed during the rainy season. ‘Varṣiṣṭham’ means exceedingly abundant and flourishing.

27.word_for_word: वनौकसः पुलिन्दीः प्रमुदिताः — the forest-dwelling Pulinda women were delighted; भगवान् ददृशे — Bhagavān saw them; वन-राजीः मधु-च्युतः — rows of forest vegetation dripping honey; गिरेः सकाशात् जल-धाराः — streams of water flowing from the mountain; तासां नादात् आसन्नाः गुहाः — caves nearby, resonant with their sound; यद् वा — alternatively; वनौकसः प्रमुदिताः आसन् — the forest dwellers were delighted; वन-राजयः मधु-च्युतः आसन् — the forest rows were dripping honey; गिरेः जल-धाराः आसन् — streams descended from the mountain; तान् सर्वतः ददर्श — Bhagavān saw all these on every side; धाराणां नादान् गुहाः च — the sounds of the streams and the caves as well
27.translation: Bhagavān saw the delighted Pulinda women who dwelt in the forest, rows of forest growth dripping honey, streams of water descending from the mountain, and nearby caves resounding with the noise of those streams. Alternatively, the syntax may be distributed as follows: the forest dwellers were delighted, the rows of trees dripped honey, and streams flowed down the mountain. Bhagavān looked upon all these everywhere, together with the roar of the streams and the caves.

32.word_for_word: अथ शरदं वर्णयति — now he describes autumn; एवं निवसतोः इति अष्टादशभिः — in eighteen verses beginning 'evaṃ nivasatoḥ'; व्यभ्रा — cloudless; विगतानि अभ्राणि यस्याः — whose clouds have gone; स्वच्छानि अम्बूनि यस्याम् — whose waters are clear; अपरुषः शान्तः अनिलः यस्याम् — whose wind is gentle and peaceful
32.translation: He now describes autumn in eighteen verses beginning with ‘evaṃ nivasatoḥ.’ ‘Vyabhrā’ means cloudless, the clouds having departed; its waters were clear, and its wind was gentle and calm.

33.word_for_word: नीरजानाम् उत्पत्तिः यया — by which lotuses arose; तया शरदा कृत्वा — by means of that autumn; नीरजानाम् उत्पत्त्या वा — or, by the arising of the lotuses
33.translation: The construction may mean ‘by that autumn which caused the lotuses to arise,’ or simply ‘through the arising of the lotuses.’

34.word_for_word: व्योम्नः अब्दम् इति — beginning with the cloud from the sky; व्योम-आदीनां चतुर्णां चतुरः मलान् शरत् अहरत् — autumn removed four impurities from four things beginning with the sky; आश्रमिणां चतुर्णां कृष्णे जाता भक्तिः यथा अशुभम् असुखं हरति — just as devotion to Kṛṣṇa removes the impurity and misery of the four āśramas; ब्रह्मचारिणः गुरु-अर्थ-उदक-आहरण-आदि-कष्टम् — the brahmacārin's hardship of fetching water and other service for the guru; भक्तिः हरति — devotion removes it; गृहिणः अपत्य-आदि-साङ्कर्यम् — the householder's entanglement with children and the like; विविक्त-वास-रुचि-उत्पत्तेः — by producing a taste for solitary dwelling; वनस्थस्य मल-धारण-क्लेशम् — the forest-dweller's trouble of bearing dirt; यतीनां काम-आदि-वासनाम् — the renunciant's latent desires beginning with lust; व्योम्नः अब्दम् — clouds from the sky; भूतानां शाबल्यम् — the motley mixture of living beings; भुवः पङ्कम् — mud from the earth; अपां मलम् — impurity from the waters
34.translation: The verse beginning with the cloud in the sky describes four impurities that autumn removes from four corresponding things, just as devotion to Kṛṣṇa removes the inauspiciousness and suffering associated with the four āśramas. For a brahmacārin, devotion removes the hardship of fetching water and performing other services for the guru, because one fulfilled by devotion no longer requires such discipline and the guru no longer assigns it to one who has attained the goal. For a householder, devotion removes entanglement with children and the like by producing a taste for secluded life. For a forest-dweller it removes the hardship represented by the accumulation of dirt; and for a renunciant it removes latent desires such as lust. Correspondingly, autumn removed the clouds from the sky, the confused mingling of creatures, the mud from the earth, and the impurity from the waters.

35.word_for_word: त्यक्त-एषणाः — those who have abandoned desires; त्यक्ताः पुत्र-वित्त-लोक-एषणाः यैः — by whom the desires for children, wealth and worlds have been given up
35.translation: ‘Tyaktaiṣaṇāḥ’ means those who have abandoned the three pursuits: desire for children, for wealth and for heavenly worlds.

36.word_for_word: गिरयः इति — with the mountains; ज्ञानिनः ज्ञान-अमृतं न सर्वतः वितरन्ति — knowers do not distribute the nectar of knowledge indiscriminately everywhere; उपाध्यायाः कर्म-विद्याम् इव — unlike ordinary teachers distributing instruction in ritual; कृपया क्वचित् एव — only in certain places, through compassion; गिरयः शिवं निर्मलं तोयं क्वचित् मुमुचुः क्वचित् न — mountains released pure auspicious water in some places and not in others; न पुनः प्रावृषि इव सर्वतः — not everywhere as during the rains
36.translation: The sense of the comparison with the mountains is this: knowers of truth do not distribute the nectar of knowledge everywhere in the manner that ordinary teachers distribute instruction in ritual; out of compassion they bestow it only in appropriate places. Similarly, in autumn the mountains released pure, auspicious water here and there, and not everywhere as they had in the rainy season.

37.word_for_word: गाधे क्षुद्रे जले चरन्ति — they move in shallow, scant water; ते मीन-आदयः — those fish and similar creatures
37.translation: The fish and other aquatic creatures meant here are those moving about in shallow, diminishing water.

38.word_for_word: अविन्दन् — they obtained; लेभिरे — they gained
38.translation: ‘Avindan’ simply means that they obtained or gained it.

39.word_for_word: शनैः शनैः — gradually, little by little; तत्र ममताम् इव पङ्कम् — mud like possessiveness; अहन्ताम् इव आमताम् अपक्वताम् — unripe condition like egoity; जहुः — they gave up
39.translation: ‘Gradually, gradually’: there the waters and land gave up their mud, compared to possessiveness, and their raw or unripe condition, compared to egoity.

40.word_for_word: आत्मनि उपरते त्यक्त-क्रिये मुनिः इव — like a sage who has withdrawn into the Self and abandoned activity; निश्चल-अम्बुः — whose water is motionless; स एव — that same body of water; व्युपरत-आगमः — with incoming streams ceased; निवृत्त-वेद-घोषः इव — like one in whom the recitation of the Veda has ceased; तूष्णीम् अभूत् — became silent
40.translation: A body of water became motionless like a sage who has withdrawn into the Self and given up external activity. With the streams flowing into it having ceased, it became silent, like a sage in whom even the audible recitation of the Veda has fallen quiet.

41.word_for_word: केदारेभ्यः — from cultivated plots; बद्धे सेतु-शालि-क्षेत्रेभ्यः — from rice fields enclosed by embankments; दृढैः सेतुभिः अपः अगृह्णन् — they retained the waters with firm dams; ततः परं वृष्टि-अभावात् — because thereafter there would be no rain; प्राणैः इन्द्रियैः — by the prāṇas, meaning the senses; तत्-निरोधेन — by restraining them; इन्द्रिय-प्रत्याहारेण — by withdrawal of the senses
41.translation: Farmers retained the water in the rice fields, which were enclosed by firm embankments, because thereafter the rains would cease. The comparison is to preserving inner vitality by restraining the prāṇas—that is, the senses—through pratyāhāra, the withdrawal of the senses.

42.word_for_word: देह-अभिमान-जं — arising from identification with the body; बोधः इव — like knowledge that removes it; व्रज-योषिताम् मुकुन्दः इव — and like Mukunda for the women of Vraja
42.translation: The intended comparisons are: like true knowledge in relation to the distress arising from identification with the body, and like Mukunda in relation to the women of Vraja.

43.word_for_word: शरदा विमलाः तारकाः यस्मिन् — in which the stars were made clear by autumn; शब्द-ब्रह्मणः वेदस्य अर्थान् — the meanings of the verbal Brahman, the Veda; पूर्व-उत्तर-मीमांसा-निर्णीतान् — as ascertained by the Pūrva- and Uttara-Mīmāṃsā; दर्शयति — makes manifest; तद्वत् — similarly
43.translation: The sky is described as having stars made clear by autumn. The comparison is to one who makes manifest the meanings of the verbal Brahman, the Veda, as determined through Pūrva- and Uttara-Mīmāṃsā. The explanation extends through verse 44.

45.word_for_word: समः — even, balanced; अन्यून-अधिकः — neither deficient nor excessive; शीतः च उष्णः च — in cold and heat; न तु गोप्यः — but not so for the gopīs; कृष्ण-अपहृत-चेतस्त्वेन — because Kṛṣṇa had stolen their minds; तासां सन्तापः दुःसहः — their burning distress was unbearable; यद् वा — alternatively; न-कारः उपमा-अर्थः — the negative particle may introduce a comparison; कृष्ण-हृत-चेतसः — their hearts stolen by Kṛṣṇa; चेतसा कृष्णम् आश्लिष्य यथा — as though embracing Kṛṣṇa with the mind
45.translation: ‘Sama’ means even and balanced, neither deficient nor excessive in cold or heat. But this balance did not apply to the gopīs: because Kṛṣṇa had stolen their minds, their burning separation was unbearable. Alternatively, the negative particle may function in a comparative sense: with their hearts stolen by Kṛṣṇa, it was as though they embraced Kṛṣṇa inwardly with the mind.

46.word_for_word: पुष्पिण्यः — flowering; गर्भिण्यः — pregnant, bearing fruit; अन्वीयमानाः स्व-वृषैः स्व-पतिभिः — being followed by their own bulls, their mates; अनिच्छन्त्यः अपि बलात् अनुगम्यमानाः — followed forcibly even when unwilling; ईश्वर-आराधन-अर्थाः क्रियाः — acts performed for the worship of the Lord; बलात् फलैः अनुगम्यमानाः — inevitably followed by their fruits; समस्त-भोग-गर्भाः यथा — as though pregnant with every enjoyment
46.translation: ‘Puṣpiṇyaḥ’ means flowering, and therefore ‘pregnant,’ bearing fruit. The cows were followed by their own bulls, their mates, even when they did not desire it. The comparison is to acts undertaken for worship of the Lord: their fruits follow them irresistibly, as though those acts were pregnant with all forms of enjoyment.

47.word_for_word: कुमुत् — kumud, the night-blooming lotus; कुमुदम् — the kumuda flower; कुत्सिता मुत् यस्य — one whose joy is base or wicked; दस्यु-साम्यम् — this gives the comparison with a thief or robber
47.translation: ‘Kumut’ refers first to the kumuda, the night-blooming lotus. By wordplay it can also mean one whose delight is base or wicked, supplying the comparison with a robber.

48.word_for_word: आग्रयणैः — by āgrayaṇa rites; नव-अन्न-प्राशन-अर्थ-वैदिकैः — Vedic observances for first eating the new grain; ऐन्द्रियैः इन्द्रिय-अर्थैः लौकिकैः च महोत्सवैः — and great worldly festivals serving the senses and their objects; कलाभ्यां राम-कृष्णाभ्यां — by the two manifestations, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa; दर्शन-आदि-महोत्सवाभ्याम् — through the great festivals of seeing them and the like
48.translation: The season was celebrated with āgrayaṇa rites, the Vedic observances connected with first eating the new grain, and with great worldly festivals devoted to the senses and their objects. Above all, the presence of the two divine manifestations, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, made the very act of seeing them and similar encounters into a supreme festival.

49.word_for_word: वणिजः यतयः नृपाः स्नातकाः च — merchants, renunciants, kings and graduates; दृष्ट-अदृष्टाभ्यां वर्ष-रुद्धाः — prevented during the rains for visible and scriptural reasons; निर्गम्य — setting out; अर्थान् — their respective aims; वाणिज्य-स्वाच्छन्द्य-दिग्-विजय-विद्या-आदीन् — trade, freedom of wandering, conquest of the directions, study and so forth; प्रपेदिरे — attained or pursued; यथा मन्त्र-योग-आदि-सिद्धाः — like those perfected through mantra, yoga and the like; आयुषा रुद्धाः — confined by the span of life; काले आगते — when the proper time comes; स्व-पिण्डान् — their own desired embodied states; योग-आदि-प्राप्यान् देवादि-देहान् — divine and other bodies obtainable through yoga and so forth
49.translation: Merchants, renunciants, kings and students who had completed their formal study had been held back during the rainy season for both practical and scripturally prescribed reasons. When autumn came they set out and pursued their respective aims—trade, freedom to wander, conquest, further learning and so forth. The comparison is to adepts perfected through mantra, yoga and similar disciplines: although confined for a time by the present span of life, when the proper moment comes they obtain the embodied states they have sought, such as divine bodies attainable through yoga.
